summary: Field runs SuperCollider's language interpreter, sclang, in two places: to render every supercollider: entry in field build, and to run the voice host that field keys plays an instrument through. Both find sclang with one function, sclangCommand in src/generators/supercollider.ts. On Windows that function could not find a real sclang even with SuperCollider installed, so renders and field keys stopped there.

This pull request makes the lookup platform-aware. On Windows it searches PATH for sclang with each PATHEXT extension, reads a native FIELD_SCLANG such as C:\Program Files\SuperCollider-3.13.0\sclang.exe as a path, and falls back to the newest SuperCollider-<version> folder under Program Files. macOS and Linux keep the lookup they had. The platform becomes a parameter of sclangCommand, so a new test file runs the Windows rules on any machine.

The review found two problems, both on Windows. The lookup can return a .cmd or .bat script, which Node refuses to start without a shell. And two of the new tests build fixtures that a Windows file system cannot hold, so the windows CI job fails them.

cards.title: Where the lookup looks, in order
cards.html:
StepmacOS and LinuxWindows
FIELD_SCLANG setA value with / is a path; a bare name is searched on PATHA value with \, /, or : is a path; a bare name is searched on PATH with each PATHEXT extension
PATHsclang in each :-separated directorysclang plus each PATHEXT extension in each ;-separated directory, never the bare name
Installed copyThe app bundle, on macOS onlyThe newest SuperCollider-<version>\sclang.exe under ProgramFiles

A FIELD_SCLANG that names nothing is an error, never a fall through to the installed copy, so a mistyped wrapper cannot silently run a different sclang.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One review at 603c3e1: changes requested, with two open findings.
  • The lookup returns scripts Node cannot start. PATHEXT includes .BAT and .CMD, and both callers spawn without a shell.
  • Two new tests fail on Windows. Their fixtures hold a drive path that a POSIX rule or a Windows file system cannot.
  • The linux CI job passes. The windows job fails 13 tests: the two new ones, and 11 that also fail on main.

groups.title: The sclang lookup
groups.kicker: One function decides which sclang a render and the voice host run, now per platform.
intro: sclangCommand returns the path of the sclang to run. runScProgram starts it with execFile for a render, and VoiceHost.start starts it with spawn for field keys. Neither caller uses a shell, so the path must name a program Windows can start directly.

Three helpers carry the Windows rules. variable reads an environment variable without regard to case on Windows, because Windows spells PATH as Path and a copied environment loses the case-insensitive lookup that process.env has. onPath searches PATH, trying each PATHEXT extension on Windows. installedSclang finds the copy the SuperCollider installer put in place: the app bundle on macOS, or the newest versioned folder under Program Files on Windows.

checks.text: PATHEXT is the Windows list of extensions that the command shell treats as runnable, by default .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD. Node can start only .com and .exe without a shell.

files.note: The platform-aware lookup: three new helpers and a platform parameter on sclangCommand.

checks.text: macOS and Linux keep their behavior. I called the built sclangCommand with linux and darwin against temporary files, and it returned what main returns: a FIELD_SCLANG with / is a path, a bare name is searched on a :-split PATH, and only macOS falls back to the app bundle. The one difference is that Linux no longer checks the macOS bundle path, which cannot exist there.
Copied environments work. With the keys spelled Path, PathExt, and programfiles, the lookup still found sclang.exe in my probe.

The lookup can return a script field cannot start. The default PATHEXT includes .BAT and .CMD, so FIELD_SCLANG=sclang-wrapper resolves to sclang-wrapper.cmd, and a sclang.cmd on PATH wins over the Program Files fallback. Node refuses to start a .bat or .cmd without a shell and throws spawn EINVAL, so a render fails with sclang failed for <program>: spawn EINVAL where main said FIELD_SCLANG points at a missing binary. The review asks to try only .com and .exe on Windows.
Versions sort as numbers. Under a fake Program Files holding SuperCollider-3.9, 3.10, 3.13.0, and an empty 3.14.0, the lookup returned 3.13.0; with only 3.9 and 3.10, it returned 3.10.
ProgramW6432 is not read. Node publishes no 32-bit Windows build from version 23 on, so for field's process ProgramFiles already names the 64-bit folder.

groups.title: Tests for each platform's rules
groups.kicker: A new test file runs the Windows rules on any machine; one comment in the build tests catches up.
intro: Because sclangCommand takes the platform as a parameter, src/generators/supercollider.test.ts passes 'win32' or 'linux' and checks the result against real files in a temporary directory. That lets the macOS and Linux CI jobs run the Windows rules too.
The catch is the other direction. On the windows CI job, the platform parameter does not change the host's own paths, so a fixture built for a POSIX rule or a POSIX file system can fail there.

files.note: Eight lookup tests, one per rule. Six pass on Windows; two fail there.

checks.text: Two tests fail on the Windows CI job. This one passes a C:\…\bin directory as PATH under the linux rule, which splits it at the colon, so it throws sclang not found on PATH. The test at line 54 writes its decoy under a directory named C:, which Windows refuses with ENOENT. The review asks to skip both on Windows, as build.test.ts skips its POSIX stubs.
This test asserts that the lookup returns sclang-wrapper.cmd, the result that the flag on supercollider.ts line 85 says Node cannot start.
On macOS all eight tests pass: pnpm exec vitest run src/generators/supercollider.test.ts.

files.note: A comment stops saying that a real sclang cannot reach this spawn on Windows.

checks.text: The supercollider and runScProgram edges tests pass on macOS: 7 run, with the real-sclang integration test left out.

Just below this hunk, sclangPresent still decides with the POSIX rules whether to run the real-sclang integration test, so that test skips on a Windows machine with SuperCollider installed. The review lists switching it to sclangCommand() as a suggestion.

groups.title: Docs and the plan
groups.kicker: The CLI manual, the keys guide, and the Windows plan describe the new order.
intro: docs/cli.md and docs/keys.md say where field build and field keys find sclang, now including sclang.exe and the Program Files folder. The Windows portability plan marks its §7.2 item, sclangCommand cannot find sclang on Windows, as ported.

checks.text: I read each doc change against sclangCommand at this head, and each matches the code. The plan stays in-progress, and project check passes.

§7.2 records the item as ported, with the rules it now follows.
